subject: Session-affinity / temporary priority override for OrbitPay PoC
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Session-affinity / temporary priority override for OrbitPay PoC

Hi team,

OrbitPay (contact: Kate O'Neil) is in week-2 of the PoC and they keep hitting a mid-stream disconnect that correlates with variant routing spikes. They repro reliably when they open long-lived streaming sessions (>2 minutes) while their traffic mixes both short generation and streaming workflows.

Why this is urgent: OrbitPay is evaluating SLA language for our Dedicated offering; if we can't stabilize the PoC by their exec review next week we risk losing the expansion. Kate is polite but blunt — she asked for a short-term operational guarantee.

Ask: can runtime provide a temporary "priority override" or session-affinity escape hatch we can enable for OrbitPay's project id so their streaming sessions are routed to a single variant/pool for the duration of the PoC? Ideally this would be a knob we set from the console (or via an emergency API flag) that pins sessions to one variant to avoid in-flight variant handoffs.

Constraints to consider:
- We need this live for a handful of sessions (non-prod PoC traffic) by EOD Tuesday PT.
- Any approach must have a clear rollback path and observability (per-session tracing and drop metrics).
- If a code change is required, a config-only option (routing policy override) is strongly preferred.

I attached the repro logs and the MAP with customer timelines. Proposed quick path:
1) Dev: confirm whether a routing rule override is possible without a full deploy.
2) Runtime/Product: evaluate risk and approve a 48-72h exception.
3) Sales Eng (Marissa/Chloe): communicate SLA guardrails to OrbitPay and schedule live repro with Runtime on Monday.

Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: orbitpay-repro-logs.tar.gz (log bundle), orbitpay-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session-affinity / temporary priority override for OrbitPay PoC

On Sun, Jun 13, 2027 at 10:12 AM Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com> wrote:
> OrbitPay (contact: Kate O'Neil) is in week-2 of the PoC and they keep hitting a mid-stream disconnect that correlates with variant routing spikes.

Thanks for the detailed repro, Chloe. I've pulled the logs. Quick summary of what I'm seeing: there are multiple small variant evictions triggered by our capacity balancer for the tenant during bursts; when a session's routing metadata changes mid-stream we drop the in-flight connection because the KV cache isn't moved between variants.

Options I see (short-term to long-term):
A) Config override at route-level: mark OrbitPay's project id as "session_invariant=true" so the router pins all new connections to a single variant. No code deploy required if we expose the flag through the internal routing table (we can). Limit: this creates uneven load distribution; we should throttle concurrent pinned sessions.

B) SDK-side escape hatch: add a header X-Session-Invariant that forces the gateway to keep connections sticky for that token. This requires a small gateway change and a one-day rollout. Backwards compatible if default is off.

C) Architectural fix: snapshot/transfer KV cache during variant migration — requires runtime work and a multi-week schedule.

Recommendation: go with (A) for the immediate window plus (B) as a 1-day follow-up to give customers programmatic control. We'll add per-session tracing so we can revert if there are resource problems.

I'll create the routing rule and add a per-tenant throttle. Need product sign-off on the exception and an ops runbook for rollback.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Attachments referenced: stability-snapshot-20270613.png
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session-affinity / temporary priority override for OrbitPay PoC

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 9:07 AM Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recommendation: go with (A) for the immediate window plus (B) as a 1-day follow-up to give customers programmatic control.

Agree with Dev's sequencing. A couple product notes / guardrails to make this safe for customers and the platform: 
1) Exemption criteria: only allow session_invariant for POCs or Dedicated customers with an approved exception document (Marissa, please attach the MAP).
2) Quota controls: limit pinned sessions per-tenant (suggest 8 concurrent pinned streams) and set an alert if pinned sessions exceed 70% of a variant's capacity.
3) Observability: require per-session trace id and a nightly summary report for any tenant using the override. We'll expose a dashboard tile in Console under the customer's project.
4) API/SDK follow-up: if we push header-based escape hatch (X-Session-Invariant), we should land it behind a feature flag in SDK v2.3 to avoid surprising older clients.

Operational ask: Sean/Runtime Ops, please prepare a short rollback MOP (runbook) and a canary plan (10% traffic, monitor errors/latency for 30m) before we flip the flag. If Ops sees any memory pressure or unusual eviction patterns, revert immediately.

I'll coordinate product sign-off—Marissa, can you open the exception request in the internal tracker and attach the MAP + customer approval email?

- Logan
Director, Product Management (API/Platform)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session-affinity / temporary priority override for OrbitPay PoC

Thanks all — thumbs up from Sales Eng and Legal has provisionally approved a 72h operational exception to support OrbitPay's executive demo. I've uploaded the signed MAP and Kate's approval email to the Drive link (see related_links).

Actions taken (owner / ETA):
- Marissa: Created internal exception in RUNTIME-911 with attachments and set it to review by product leadership (DONE).
- Dev: Please create the routing-table override and limit to 6 concurrent pinned sessions for the tenant. Requesting ETA: EOD Monday (14-Jun) — Dev reported he can do this, please confirm once applied.
- Sean: Prepare rollback MOP and alerting (ETA: EOD Monday).
- Logan: Flag Console tile for per-tenant override metrics — best-effort minimal telemetry by Tuesday morning.
- Chloe: I'll coordinate the live repro session with OrbitPay and have them land their PoC traffic on the pinned route.

Risk notes for the record: this is an operational exception that increases single-variant load; we accept temporary uneven capacity distribution to preserve PoC success. Post-PoC we'll revert and prioritize the architectural KV-transfer fix.

Marissa Cole
Sales Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
